title: Kenyan Roasted Goat Ribs
community: A favourite across all communities — especially at outdoor celebrations
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Roasted Goat Ribs — mbavu za mbuzi rubbed with a simple blend of garlic, ginger, salt, and pepper, then slow-roasted over charcoal until the fat renders, the skin crisps, and the meat falls tenderly from the bone. Pure, honest Kenyan barbecue.
longDesc: Goat ribs are one of the great Kenyan outdoor cooking experiences. The fat that runs through the ribs bastes the meat as it cooks over charcoal, the edges caramelise and char lightly, and the meat — when given enough time — becomes impossibly tender. Eaten directly from the bone with kachumbari and ugali, it is Kenyan barbecue at its most elemental.
ingredients: 1.5 kg goat ribs — cut into sections
steps: Mix garlic, ginger, salt, pepper, paprika, cumin, oil, and lemon juice into a paste.
Rub the paste thoroughly over all surfaces of the goat ribs. Marinate for 1 hour at room temperature or overnight in the refrigerator.
Light the charcoal. Allow to burn to glowing coals with a light layer of white ash — not open flames.
Place the ribs on the grill over medium-low charcoal heat.
Roast for 35—45 minutes, turning every 8—10 minutes, until the outside is browned and slightly charred and the meat is tender.
The ribs are ready when the meat pulls easily from the bone.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with kachumbari and ugali.
chefTips: Low and slow is the rule for ribs — cook over medium heat, not high, to render the fat without burning.
The ribs are done when the meat begins to pull back from the bone tips.
A baste of the leftover marinade (boiled first for safety) applied during the last 10 minutes adds a beautiful caramelised gloss.
commonMistakes: Cooking over high heat — burns the outside before the inside is tender.
Turning too frequently — prevents proper crust formation.

faqs.q: Can I cook these in the oven?
faqs.a: Yes — roast at 180°C for 60—75 minutes, uncovered, turning halfway. For extra tenderness, wrap in foil for the first 45 minutes, then unwrap to brown.

cookingScience: Goat ribs contain significant collagen in the connective tissue between and around the bones. Slow roasting at moderate heat converts this collagen to gelatin over time, producing the characteristic fall-off-the-bone tenderness. High heat hardens the protein too quickly for collagen breakdown to occur.
sustainabilityTips: Using the whole rib section — bones, fat, and meat — makes full use of the animal.
Gnaw the bones — they are rich in marrow.
reheating: Reheat in oven at 180°C for 10 minutes.
healthBenefits: High in protein and rich in collagen from the bone-in preparation.
Goat fat has a healthier fatty acid profile than beef or lamb fat.
culturalNote: Roasted goat ribs are a centrepiece of Kenyan outdoor gatherings, community events, and family celebrations. The smell of goat ribs over charcoal is one of the most evocative aromas in Kenyan outdoor food culture.
regionalVariations: Plain salt-rubbed ribs — the Maasai tradition.
Heavily spiced ribs — northern Kenyan style.
Lemon and herb ribs — coastal variation.
